title: Part 830: NTSB Accident Reporting
description: NTSB accident and incident definitions, notification requirements, and reporting procedures

cards.back:
An occurrence associated with aircraft operation from boarding to deplaning resulting in:

• Death
• Serious injury
• Substantial damage to aircraft

All three elements: occurrence + operation period + result

Damage that adversely affects:
• Structural strength
• Performance
• Flight characteristics

AND requires major repair or component replacement

Exclusions: Engine damage, bent fairings, small holes, landing gear, prop/rotor blades

• Engine damage (engine only)
• Bent fairings or cowling
• Dented skin
• Small puncture holes
• Damage to landing gear
• Damage to wheels, tires, flaps
• Damage to propeller/rotor blades
• Damage to accessories (antennas, lights)

• Hospitalization >48 hours (within 7 days of injury)
• Bone fracture (except simple nose/finger/toe)
• Severe hemorrhage
• Nerve, muscle, or tendon damage
• Internal organ injury
• 2nd/3rd degree burns >5% of body

IMMEDIATELY notify NTSB

By most expeditious means available (usually telephone)

NTSB Response Center: 1-844-373-9922

Within 10 DAYS of accident

Form: NTSB Form 6120.1/2

Incidents: Only when NTSB requests

The OPERATOR of the aircraft

Operator = person who causes or authorizes operation

Usually: Owner, lessee, or person exercising operational control

• Flight control malfunction/failure
• Inability of required crew to perform duties (incapacitation)
• In-flight fire
• Aircraft collision in flight
• Damage to property >$25,000
• Overdue aircraft believed in accident
• Release of propeller blade
• Turbine engine debris escape

• Complete loss of flight recorder info
• TCAS Resolution Advisory in RVSM airspace
• Aircraft evacuation using emergency egress
• Emergency descent from flight crew oxygen deficiency
• Runway incursion requiring evasive action

• Type/registration of aircraft
• Name of owner/operator
• Name of PIC
• Date and time of accident
• Last departure point and intended destination
• Position of aircraft
• Number of persons aboard
• Injuries and fatalities
• Nature of accident and damage

Operator must preserve wreckage, mail, and cargo until NTSB takes custody

May move ONLY to:
• Protect wreckage from further damage
• Remove persons (injured or deceased)
• Protect public from injury

Before moving, document:
• Sketches of original positions
• Descriptive notes
• Photographs

Preserve condition of wreckage as much as possible

ACCIDENT: Results in death, serious injury, or substantial damage

INCIDENT: Occurrence other than accident that affects or could affect safety

Some incidents require immediate notification (see list)

Engine failure alone is NOT automatically reportable

Becomes ACCIDENT if results in:
• Death
• Serious injury
• Substantial damage

Forced landing with no damage/injury = no report required

Usually NOT substantial damage if only:
• Landing gear damaged
• Propeller damaged
• Skin scraped/dented

Becomes accident if structural damage or injury occurs

NTSB:
• Investigates accidents
• Determines probable cause
• Makes safety recommendations

FAA:
• Enforces regulations
• Takes certificate action
• Implements safety changes

NTSB is independent of FAA

IMMEDIATELY notify NTSB of:
• Any ACCIDENT
• Specific INCIDENTS (fire, collision, control failure, etc.)

10 DAYS: Written report for accidents

Remember: When in doubt, report!

Immediately reportable incident:

'Inability of any required flight crewmember to perform normal flight duties as a result of injury or illness'

Includes: Heart attack, stroke, loss of consciousness, severe illness

Immediately reportable incident:

Damage to property OTHER than aircraft exceeds $25,000

Examples: Hangar damage, vehicle damage, building damage

Immediately reportable:

'An aircraft is overdue and is believed to have been involved in an accident'

Notify NTSB even before confirmation of accident

Immediately reportable incident:

'Flight control system malfunction or failure'

Includes: Jammed controls, cable failure, hydraulic failure affecting controls, autopilot malfunction

Immediately reportable incident:

'In-flight fire'

Includes: Engine fire, electrical fire, cabin fire

Report regardless of whether fire was extinguished or damage occurred

Immediately reportable incident:

'Aircraft collision in flight'

Report regardless of damage or injury

Includes: Any contact between aircraft in flight

24-Hour Response Center:
1-844-373-9922

Online: www.ntsb.gov

Form 6120.1: Available online

When in doubt, CALL!

Death within 30 days of accident

Death directly resulting from:
• Injuries sustained
• Damage to aircraft

Excludes: Natural causes, self-inflicted, inflicted by others
